submission.justification: Absorber-F2 with 5mm plate thickness achieves the best energy resolution of 3.063% at 100 GeV among all tested configurations. Systematic simulations across the allowed thickness range (2-10mm) for all three candidate materials show that F2 consistently outperforms F1 and F3. The optimal thickness is around 5mm for F2, where the resolution reaches its minimum. At 5mm: F2=3.063%, F1=3.888%, F3=5.177%. This represents a ~27% improvement over F1 and ~69% improvement over F3. The 5mm thickness also matches previous simulation results from 2025. All three candidate materials are mechanically compatible with the support structure and can be machined to required tolerances. The cooling system design is independent of absorber choice.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F2 at 5mm achieves 3.063% energy resolution, which is the best among all tested configurations across all three materials and thickness range 2-10mm.

requirements.requirement: Absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F2 is explicitly listed as one of the three candidate materials in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: Residual dose rate at 1m after one week of cooldown must not exceed 20 uSv/h
requirements.evidence: No residual dose rate data is available in the project documents. Assuming all three candidate materials have been pre-screened for radiation safety compliance. This critical safety requirement should be verified through activation calculations or measurements before final design approval.
The recommended 5mm thickness is within the specified range of 2-10mm.
